page: Amazon Web Services c8g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading resource sharing. The system is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but delivers a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, particularly in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core suites. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, reaching 480.57 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. The server also excels in database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations, placing in the top 10% of tested configurations. Single-core performance is strong but comparatively moderate, aligning with the average to strong tiers in single-threaded tasks.

The dedicated core allocation and high memory bandwidth provide excellent qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized, compute-bound workloads. By avoiding hyperthreading, the instance ensures predictable execution times for demanding tasks. This profile is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-to-large scale LLM text generation tasks where GPU acceleration is not required.
